facts.content: Chief complaint is progressive numbness and tingling in the left arm for 2 weeks.
facts.source_text: CC: Progressive numbness/tingling L arm (2 wks)

facts.content: Left arm numbness and tingling started after the patient began a boxing class.
Left arm symptoms have worsened despite massage and hot baths.
The patient reports mild weakness in the left arm with difficulty playing the piano.
The numbness and tingling involve the palmar side of the second to fourth digits and extend from the elbow to the hand.
facts.source_text: distribution—2nd-4th digits, palmar side, extends elbow→hand

facts.content: The patient has occasional shoulder pain associated with the arm symptoms.
The patient denies neck pain.
The patient had an upper respiratory infection or flu one month ago that lasted about two weeks.
facts.source_text: Recent illness: URI/“flu” 1 mo ago (2 wks duration)

facts.content: The patient reports no significant past medical history.
The patient takes ibuprofen as needed.
The patient takes vitamin D.
The patient takes iron inconsistently.
The patient uses melatonin as needed.
The patient's father has hypothyroidism and an autoimmune condition.
The patient's mother has type 2 diabetes.
The patient's mother has hypertension.
The patient's mother has hyperlipidemia.
The patient participates in boxing classes and regular workouts.
The patient has occasional episodes of heavy alcohol use during parties.
The patient is right-hand dominant.
Left upper limb paresthesia and mild weakness with differential diagnoses including multiple sclerosis, peripheral neuropathy, cervical radiculopathy, or overuse.

facts.content: Transient monocular visual deficit considered possible optic neuritis with need to rule out demyelinating disease.

facts.content: An urgent neurology referral is planned for MRI of the brain and spine and a full neurological work-up.

facts.content: The patient was educated on red-flag symptoms including increased weakness, leg involvement, new visual loss, headache, vomiting, and seizures requiring emergency department evaluation.

facts.content: The patient is advised to continue over-the-counter analgesia with ibuprofen as needed and to start no new medications until neurology review.

facts.content: The patient is encouraged to remain active within comfort and avoid aggravating boxing drills.
